name: Flagger (symbol)
spec: orange diamond with a black flagger-holding-flag symbol
meaning: A flagger is directing traffic ahead; obey the paddle or flag.

snippets.back: A flagger-ahead warning tells drivers to prepare to stop.
A flagger is a person who directs work-area traffic using a flag or sign.
Stop no closer than fifteen feet from the nearest rail when you see flashing red lights, a lowered barricade, ringing bells or a flagger warning of a train or other on-track equipment.

Work zones demand slowing, wider gaps, and full attention past cones and flaggers with early merges; violations cost one thousand-plus, fines double in enhanced or staffed zones, worker assault risks two thousand and a year inside, and drivers move over for amber-lit rigs.
Large projects may use flaggers, portable concrete barriers, complex signs and reduced speed limits, and those lower limits give drivers more time to read and react.

Orange diamond or square work boards warn of crews, slow detours, crawling machines and shifting pavement, detour boards open the backup path, and flaggers in bright vests with paddles and red flags rule the zone absolutely.
Work-zone flaggers may stop, slow or direct traffic to move it safely through the site.
Obey work-zone warning signs and directions given by flaggers, cones, and barrels.

result.summary: Meaning supported: snippets define flagger as directing work-area traffic with flag/sign, to be obeyed, and flagger-ahead means prepare to stop. No snippet describes an orange diamond with black flagger-holding-flag symbol, only generic orange diamond/square work boards.
